o: Recognise the purpose of standard OCR J277 flowchart symbols.
Trace a Yes/No decision for two values.
Translate a simple flowchart into OCR Exam Reference Language.
c: A flowchart represents an algorithm visually. Follow arrows from Start through each process or decision until End.
Start and End use terminal shapes. Inputs and outputs use parallelograms, processes use rectangles, and decisions use diamonds. Predefined subprograms have their own symbol.
A diamond evaluates a condition. True/Yes and False/No lead down alternative routes, so a value follows only the appropriate path.
Follow the algorithm with a test value. If input is invalid, an arrow can return to input/check for another attempt. Each branch should lead to a defined next action or End.

visuals.title: BRANCH WHEN A CONDITION IS TRUE

m.title: Trace two branches
m.q: A flowchart checks if a mark is at least 5. If true it prints 'Pass'; otherwise it prints 'Try again'. Explain which branch is followed for 7 and 3. [4 marks]
st: The diamond checks mark >= 5. Only one branch is followed per test.
7 >= 5 is true [1], so the Yes branch prints Pass [1].
3 >= 5 is false [1], so the No branch prints Try again [1].
Check both comparisons and the different outputs; avoid running both branches for one input.

w: A flowchart checks whether a number is greater than 10. Explain the route and output for 12 and 8. [4 marks]
12 > 10 is true [1], follows Yes and prints High [1]. 8 > 10 is false [1], follows No and prints Low [1].
A lunch-order flowchart repeats a question after an invalid choice. Explain why an arrow loops back to the input. [4 marks]
Invalid choice follows the No route [1] and causes another input request [1]. The return arrow rechecks the new choice [1] until it is valid [1].
A flowchart uses a rectangle 'total = a + b' then a parallelogram 'Display total'. Explain both symbols. [4 marks]
Rectangle represents processing [1] calculating and storing a sum [1]. Parallelogram represents output [1], displaying the calculated total [1].
wSteps: Test the condition separately for each number.
12 > 10 is true, follow Yes and print High [2].
8 > 10 is false, follow No and print Low [2].
Return arrow repeats checking until valid [2].
Invalid follows No [1], retries [1], loops back [1], tests a new value [1].
Match each shape to its job.
Rectangle performs a calculation and assignment [2].
Process rectangle [1] calculates total [1]; output parallelogram [1] displays it [1].

k.q: Translate a simple Yes/No flowchart to OCR ERL using selection.
k.code:
age = 18
if age >= 16 then
    print("Eligible")
else
    print("Not eligible")
endif
p: Change the test to age >= 21, then predict for 18.
k.a:
Age 18 at threshold 16 prints Eligible. Age 14 prints Not eligible.

After changing condition:
age = 18
if age >= 21 then
    print("Eligible")
else
    print("Not eligible")
endif

Output: Not eligible.

Describe the purposes of terminal, input/output, process and decision symbols in flowcharts and the use of arrows. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style teaching question, not an official OCR past paper.

Terminal identifies start/end [1]; parallelogram input/output [1]; rectangle performs process/calculation [1]; diamond checks condition [1]; it directs to alternative Yes/No branches [1]; arrows show sequence/control flow [1].

A café calculates the cost of two drinks then adds a £1 service charge. Write FOUR logical steps for the algorithm. [4 marks]
Input price of drink 1 [1]; input drink 2 price [1]; total = price1 + price2 + 1 [1]; output total [1].
